# Citation checks (Chrome DevTools MCP)

1. Open `/tests/fixtures/components/citation/` on the existing Vite server. Run `await (await import('/tests/fixtures/components/citation/api.ts')).verifyCitations()` through MCP evaluation. Expect 36 assertions. Repeat with `?package` after `npm run build`.
2. At rest every citation is an outlined chip with no fill and muted text. Hover `#preview` with the real pointer: the text brightens, the border darkens, the external-link mark appears over the end of `tides.example` while the label end fades out, and the citation's width is unchanged (measure before and during hover). After the delay the preview shows the site icon, `tides.example`, the title and the description, start-aligned. Leave both the citation and the card: it closes and the mark fades out.
3. Press Tab from the page start: the preview link and the inert note show the focus ring; the link shows the mark while focused; the preview opens after the focus delay; Enter opens the site in a new tab. Tab to the footnote marker `1` and press Enter: focus moves to list entry 1 with the focus ring, and the entry's preview stays closed. Clicking the marker does the same without the ring.
4. Inspect the accessibility tree: `Citation: tides.example (opens in a new tab)`, a note named `Citation: Field interview`, the numbered markers `Citation 1: Grid storage notes (opens in a new tab)` and `Citation 2: Coastal survey 2025 (opens in a new tab)`, and a list named `Sources` with two list items.
5. Inspect light and dark themes, RTL (`dir="rtl"` on a paragraph: the mark sits at the inline end and the fade mirrors) and a 375px viewport: superscript markers do not change the line height; labelled chips ellipsize; no horizontal overflow beyond the page minimum width.
